1 · Build the test fixture

Fixture PCB with pogo pins (render of the generated .kicad_pcb)
Probe points on the board (red = supply, dark = GND, green = measured)

Parts

  • 64 x pogo pin P75 (48 spear tip, 16 crown tip)
  • 64 x receptacle R75 (fixture drill 1.40 mm)
  • 2 x J1, J2 connector: the interface of PCB TestKit catalog station 1 (footprint and pin map from the facility)
  • programming connector: 8 x copy of the board's programming header
  • 8 x nest (print, PETG)
  • 32 x M3 hex standoff, female-female, 15 mm
  • 32 x M3 x 6 screw + M3 large washer (DIN 9021, 9 mm), on top of each standoff
  • 32 x M3 x 6 screw + M3 nylon washer, standoff to fixture board (from below)
  • 32 x compression spring, outer 8 mm, wire 0.5 mm, free length 10 mm (solid 3.5 mm or less)
  • 8 x vertical toggle clamp, about 25 kg, flanged base (e.g. GH-101-A)
  • 8 x clamp adapter (print)
  • 8 x press plate (print)
  • 32 x M4 x 12 screw + M4 nut, clamp to adapter (nuts in the adapter's channels)
  • 32 x M3 x 10 screw + M3 nylon washer, adapter to fixture board from below (cuts its own thread)
  • 16 x nut + washer for the clamp's spindle, one each side of the press plate
  • 4 x M3 standoffs under the fixture board
1
sensor_20-fixture.kicad_pcb: The router left 10 of 119 connection(s) unrouted (S1_VIN, GND, S3_VIN, S4_VIN): route them in KiCad, run DRC and order it.
2
Press the receptacles into the plated holes and solder them; insert the pogo pins (crown tips on through-hole leads, spear tips on flat pads - see the probes CSV).
3
Build a nest and a clamp for every board (section below): standoffs, springs, the printed nest, the clamp on its adapter and the press plate. Mount the fixture on M3 standoffs.
4
Solder the divider resistors and the J1, J2 connector. The fixture is made for PCB TestKit catalog station 1 (fixed 300 x 220 mm plate, its mounting holes and connector position): it plugs straight in, the pin map is below.
5
The fixture takes a batch of 8 boards (4 x 2 sites, numbered row by row from the top left, S1..S8 on the silkscreen). Every site has its own header and power terminal; wire them as runner/hardware.json describes (one power switch per site).

Programming

J2 (SWD, SWD): the pogo pins reach every pin of it, and the fixture has a copy of the board's programming header per board, PRG1, PRG2, PRG3, PRG4, PRG5, PRG6, PRG7, PRG8. Plug your programmer into it while the board sits on the pins: it programs the board as if it were plugged into J2.

Connector pinSignalBoard
1VREFJ2 pin 1
2GNDJ2 pin 2
3SWDIOJ2 pin 3
4SWCLKJ2 pin 4
5NRSTJ2 pin 5

Board nest and clamp (one per board, 8 in all)

The board slides in from the front: it rests on two ledges along its edges, 1.8 mm above the pogo tips, between two rails up to the end stop. Lay it on the rails' lead-in in front of its place and slide it back to the stop. The nest floats on four sprung standoffs: closing the clamp pushes board and nest down 3.3 mm, the pins come up through the open middle of the nest and are compressed 1.5 mm.

The gap above the tips clears J1 on the board's underside while it slides in.

Nest (print with the flat side down)
Press plate (print fingers up)
Clamp adapter (print upside down)
a
Print the parts below (PETG holds its shape under the spring and clamp load), 8 of each.
b
Screw the 15 mm M3 standoffs onto the fixture board from below (the four NEST holes of every board). Slip a spring over each standoff.
c
Lay the nest on the springs with its bosses over the standoffs and screw a large washer on top of each: the springs lift the nest against the washers, 7.3 mm above the fixture.
d
Put the M4 nuts in the channels under the clamp adapter, bolt the toggle clamp onto it (the cross slots take base patterns within 4 mm of 20 x 16 mm; set fixture.nest.clamp_holes_mm for yours and reprint only the adapter), and screw the adapter to the fixture from below (the CLAMP holes).
e
Take the rubber tip off the clamp's spindle and fix the press plate in its slot with a nut on each side, fingers down, centred over the board.
f
Adjust the spindle: with a board in the nest, the clamp should lock just as the nest reaches the bottom of its travel (3.3 mm down). The fingers then press the board 1.5 mm onto the pins.

2 · Run a production test

Slide the board in along the rails to the stop: it rides above the pogo tips...
...and close its clamp: the board and nest go down, every pogo pin touches its test point
1
Copy the runner folder to the Raspberry Pi and describe your wiring in hardware.json.
2
Once, with known-good boards: python3 pcbtest_runner.py learn --units 3 to fill in signal limits.
3
For every batch: slide a board into each of the 8 nests and close its clamp, run python3 pcbtest_runner.py test --loop and enter the serial numbers. The runner checks every board unpowered and powers it up, then programs all 8 at the same time and, while the programmers run, measures what needs no firmware; the checks that need the firmware follow. A verdict per board (--site 2 retests one board, --sequential tests one board after the other).
4
Programming (step SP): when the runner asks, program the board through the fixture's PROG connector of that site with your programmer, then answer y. Set program.command to let the runner do it.
5
Green PASS: next board. Red FAIL: the failed checks are listed and stored in results/results.csv.
StepWhat is checked
S1 Visual inspectionPolarity/orientation correct, IC pin-1 orientation matches silkscreen, Through-hole joints filled, leads clipped <= 1.5 mm
S2 Unpowered short check (rails to GND)VIN_5V 100.0.., +3V3 100.0..
S3 Apply power (VIN_5V = 5.0 V)VIN_5V 4.75..5.25
SP Program the board through J2 (swd)
S4 Rail voltages+3V3 3.135..3.465
S5 Signal levels (idle)SWDIO None..None
S9 Remove power

Production timing

A batch of 8 takes about 4 min 14 s to test (32 s per board), 3 min 31 s less than one board after the other, and about 4 min 41 s to hand-solder with the jigs (2 parts, 7 joints per board, 1 jig load). Per board, everything together: 1 min 07 s.

load, check, power upprogrammingchecks while programmingchecks with firmware

Past 6 boards per batch a bigger batch saves less than 5% per board. Estimates (programming 30 s per board, set your own durations in timing in pcbtestkit.json); the runner records the real ones in every result file.

3 · Hand-solder with the jigs

Build order

PassWhatJig
1reflow the 4 SMD part(s) on the top side
2hand-solder J1, J2 (top side)jig set

Batch: every jig holds 8 board(s) (4 x 2).

3D-printed jig (192.5 x 66.0 x 17.0 mm)
place part hereclearance for assembled partsalignment post

Print sensor_20-jig.stl as it is (pockets face up, no supports): PLA or PETG, 0.2 mm layers, 3 walls. The pocket map is the jig as it lies on your desk.

Fit check passed. The jigs are cut to every part's 3D shape (KiCad's 3D export); the check compares each part with each jig.
  • top side: Fit check (10 parts, their 3D shapes): nothing touches on the way in; all 2 hand-soldered parts touch their pockets as the board lands on the support (within 0.01 mm) and are held on all four sides (0.19 to 0.23 mm of play); the holding jig closes over the placement jig without touching it. Estimated (box) shapes: TP1, TP2, TP3, TP4, U1.
1
Print both jigs as they are (no supports): sensor_20-jig-placement.stl (placement jig) and sensor_20-jig.stl (holding jig).
The two printed jigs: placement jig (left) and holding jig (right)
2
Put the PCB top side up into the placement jig; the stops around the edge locate it.
3
Fit the hand-soldered parts from above, the normal way: J1 (PWR_IN), J2 (SWD). Mind polarity marks. The leads go through their holes into the wells under the board; trim leads longer than 10 mm.
PCB top side up in the placement jig; each part goes straight down into its holes
4
Put the holding jig on top, pockets down: its posts go through the mounting holes and every part sits in its pocket.
The holding jig comes down over the parts, pockets first
5
Hold both jigs together and turn the stack over. Lift off the placement jig: every lead now points up.
Stack turned over, placement jig lifted off: the board lies in the holding jig, leads up
6
Solder all leads from above, clip them, lift the board out with the finger notches.
Solder from above; the jig holds every part flush and square
Placement jig (198.0 x 69.5 x 13.4 mm): lead wells, post holes and locating stops
